statement.p: Convert from rectangular to polar coordinates:
Note: Choose r and \theta such that r is nonnegative and 0 \leq \theta \lt 2\pi

static.solution:
\mathbf{(a)} The point (2,0) is on the positive x axis distanced 2 units from the origin. Hence, r=2 and \theta=0.
Thus, (r,\theta)=(2,0)
\mathbf{(b)} The point (12,\frac{12}{\sqrt{3}}) is in the first quadrant so \theta = \tan^{-1} \left(\frac{\frac{12}{\sqrt{3}}}{12}\right) = \frac{\pi}{6}.
Also, r=\sqrt{{12}^2+\left({\frac{12}{\sqrt{3}}}\right)^2} = \sqrt{192} Hence, (r,\theta)=\left(\sqrt{192},\frac{\pi}{6}\right)
\mathbf{(c)} The point (-3,3) is in the second quadrant. Hence, { \theta ={ \tan}^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{-3}\right) = {\tan}^{-1}(-1)=\pi -\frac{\pi }{4}=\frac{3\pi }{4}}. Also, r=\sqrt{{(-3)}^{2}+{3}^{2}}=\sqrt{18}. Hence, \left(r,\theta\right)=\left(\sqrt{18},\frac{3\pi }{4}\right).
\mathbf{(d)} The point \left(-\sqrt{3},1\right) is in the second quadrant, hence, \theta ={\tan}^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{-\sqrt{3}}\right)= \tan^{-1}\left(-\frac1{\sqrt{3}}\right)=\pi -\frac{\pi }{6}=\frac{5\pi }{6}. Also, r=\sqrt{\left(-\sqrt{3}\right)^{2}+{\left(1\right)}^{2}}=\sqrt{4}=2. Hence, \left(r,\theta \right)=\left(2,\frac{5\pi }{6}\right).
